req.title: Create form GET returns 200
req.statement: The system shall serve the create-post form at GET /create for authenticated users.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-038 requires GET /create to return HTTP 200 for authenticated users. Three test cases are needed: (1) positive — authenticated user gets 200 with form content; (2) negative — unauthenticated user is redirected (302) not served the form; (3) boundary — state transition from unauthenticated to authenticated then GET /create returns exactly 200. Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill status-code mutations, redirect-target mutations, and boolean-negation mutations on the login_required decorator.

tests.name: test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database containing seeded users
User 'Rahul' (id=1, password='stone') exists in the database
actions: POST /auth/login with username='Rahul' and password='stone' to establish session
expected: Login POST returns HTTP 302 redirect to '/'
Response body contains the create-post form (b'<form' present)
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    assert login_r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    r = client.get('/create')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'<form' in r.data

test_create_get_authenticated_returns_200()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_after_login_logout_login_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r_login1 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r_login1.status_code == 302
    r1 = client.get('/create')
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    r_logout = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert r_logout.status_code == 302
    r2 = client.get('/create')
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    assert r2.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    r_login2 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r_login2.status_code == 302
    r3 = client.get('/create')
    assert r3.status_code == 200
    assert b'<form' in r3.data

test_create_get_after_login_logout_login_returns_200()

tests.name: test_create_get_wrong_password_then_correct_returns_200
preconditions: App is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh database containing seeded users
User 'Ishaan' (id=3, password='stone') exists in the database
actions: POST /auth/login with username='Ishaan' and wrong password='wrong'
POST /auth/login with username='Ishaan' and correct password='stone'
expected: Failed login POST returns 200 (re-renders login form with error)
GET /create after failed login returns 302 to /auth/login
GET /create after successful login returns exactly 200
trace: R-FLASKR-038: boundary between failed-auth (no session) and successful-auth (session set); status flips from 302 to 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_create_get_wrong_password_then_correct_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r_bad = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'wrong'})
    assert r_bad.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in r_bad.data
    r_unauth = client.get('/create')
    assert r_unauth.status_code == 302
    assert r_unauth.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    r_good = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r_good.status_code == 302
    r_create = client.get('/create')
    assert r_create.status_code == 200
    assert b'<form' in r_create.data

test_create_get_wrong_password_then_correct_returns_200()
